title: fix(app-shell): declare the spec default for escalation.notifySubmitter in the flow-node inspector
body:
Part of #6794

The metadata-admin flow-node table declared no `defaultValue` for `escalation.notifySubmitter` while the installed `@objectstack/spec` defaults the key to `true`. One line of table data, plus the reconciliation assertion that keeps the two sides pinned.

## Premise, re-derived against the install surface

Triage asked the implementing seat to re-derive rather than trust the pin, because the pin moves. Two independent readings of the artefact a consumer actually installs, plus the runtime's own answer:

| reading | result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolution | `@objectstack/spec: 17.2.0` |
| `npm pack @objectstack/spec@17.2.0` — `package/dist/automation/index.js:3497` | `notifySubmitter: zod.z.boolean().default(true).describe(...)` |
| this worktree's installed copy — `node_modules/.pnpm/@objectstack+spec@17.2.0_ai@7.0.65_zod@4.4.3_/.../dist/automation/index.js:3497` | identical line |
| the runtime's own answer — `ApprovalEscalationSchema.safeParse({ timeoutHours: 24 })` | `{ enabled: false, timeoutHours: 24, action: 'notify', notifySubmitter: true }` |

**The premise holds: live today, not latent.** The card's collapse-into-a-duplicate branch stays closed, and the split was correct.

The same reading also re-confirms the sibling card's latency in the other direction: `enabled` is still `default(false)` in 17.2.0, so installed spec and table still agree on it.

## What changed

- `flow-node-config.ts` — `escalation.notifySubmitter` gains `defaultValue: 'true'`, with a comment naming the spec and the online half.
- `flow-node-config.spec-reconciliation.test.ts` — a new describe block. The file is already the objectui half of the form-versus-spec ledger; it carried the KEY axis, this adds the DEFAULT axis for this one field.

The expected value is **read out of the installed spec**, never spelled out as a literal: objectui consumes that contract and must not become a second source of truth for it. A vacuity guard beside it asserts the key still materialises from an omitted input, so the comparison can never quietly become a comparison against `undefined`.

A corroboration worth recording: the **online** half of this same form already carried the default. A backend that publishes the approval `configSchema` sends `default: true` for the key, and `json-schema-to-fields` turns a JSON-Schema `default` into `defaultValue: 'true'` — the fixture in `json-schema-to-fields.test.ts:68` is that exact payload. Offline and online were rendering the same key from two different claims about the spec.

## Ablation — red without the fix, green with it

Mutation and restore both proven on disk, both legs under one trap, restore pinned to the HEAD blob rather than to a bare checkout.

| leg | tree | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| green | as committed | `Test Files 1 passed (1)` · `Tests 12 passed, 1 skipped (13)` |
| red | `defaultValue: 'true'` removed | `Test Files 1 failed (1)` · `Tests 1 failed, 11 passed, 1 skipped (13)` |

The red leg's named failure is the new assertion and nothing else:

```
FAIL  packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-node-config.spec-reconciliation.test.ts
  approval escalation: declared default vs ApprovalEscalationSchema (#6794)
  the form declares the default the spec applies
AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'true'
```

The mutation was confirmed on disk before the red leg ran — anchor replaced exactly once (a zero-hit replace exits non-zero), declared-default marker count 1 to 0, bare marker count 0 to 1, blob hash `df04b55` to `93555d5`. The restore reproduced the HEAD blob `df04b55` byte-for-byte with `git diff HEAD` empty. The first attempt at this ablation **failed loudly on a bad grep anchor** rather than reporting a no-op as a measurement, which is the check working.

**No existing test moved.** Not one assertion was edited or deleted; the whole `metadata-admin` suite is green unchanged (216 files, 2264 tests). Stating it plainly because it is a real answer: this field had no default-side coverage at all, so there was nothing to update.

## Read before grading this as the p1 remedy

The card's severity narrative is that the checkbox reads unchecked while the runtime notifies. **This fix does not change what the checkbox renders**, and no fix confined to the table could:

`FlowConfigField.defaultValue` has exactly one consumer in the repo — `isFieldVisible` (`flow-node-config.ts`), which resolves an unset **controller** for `showWhen`. The render path never reads it: `FlowNodeConfigField` draws a boolean as `checked={value === true}` off the stored value alone, and no field currently gates on `notifySubmitter`. So what lands here is the **declaration** made honest — the table now states what the runtime does, the offline half agrees with the online half, and any future `showWhen` naming this controller resolves correctly.

The remaining half — ten fields in this table declare a default and the rendered control reads none of them — is filed as #6830 and deliberately not ridden in here. It also is not obviously a bug in the direction one would guess: an adjacent maintainer ruling on #6263 says the console *needs no second default contract*, so the question there is how an effective default is **shown**, not whether the designer should start writing defaults into stored metadata. That is a triage call, not this card's.

## Not absorbed

#6620 is the same class and its stated shape would have covered this field too, but it is `pm:on-hold` deliberately, behind a future spec bump that flips its own key's default. Adopting the general shape here would discharge it without its restart condition being met, so this PR does not: the new assertion is scoped to `notifySubmitter` alone, with the reason written in the test, and the sibling card is untouched and stays open. A note about the general shape belongs on that card, for its own grading.

## Verification

Union re-run after the final commit, at `7bf9a6313`:

| command | verdict line |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run` (3 inspector files, from the repo root) | `Test Files 3 passed (3)` · `Tests 84 passed, 1 skipped (85)` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` | `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run lint` | `2789 problems (0 errors, 2789 warnings)` — the package baseline; neither changed file emits a diagnostic |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | `No changeset declares a major bump` |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | `OK (scanned 5648 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)` |
| `pnpm check:designer-field-key-parity` · `check:spec-symbols` · `check:i18n-keys` · `check:i18n-drift` · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` | all exit 0 |

Tests were run **from the repo root**, the way the repo's own scripts do — `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE` re-roots at the package and is a false green here. The executed file names are in the verbose run: every one of the 13 cases is prefixed `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-node-config.spec-reconciliation.test.ts`.

The type-check was proven to actually cover both edited files rather than assumed to: `tsc --listFiles` names `flow-node-config.ts` in both projects and the new test file in `tsconfig.test.json`. The heavier runs above (type-check, lint, the 216-file suite) executed at `980a5f90c`; the only delta to `7bf9a6313` is the added changeset file, no source change.
